source.title: How does a Neural Network's Architecture Impact its Robustness to Noisy Labels?
source.authors: Jing-Ling Li; Mozhi Zhang; Keyulu Xu; John P. Dickerson; Jimmy Ba

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether architecture affects generalization-related performance under noisy labels using a linear probe of learned representations, a different measure from the catalog versions' train–test gap and most of their stated outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on raw test performance and the predictive power of representations under noisy-label training. These directly concern generalization under noisy labels and architectural conditions. Rows are limited to explicitly reported numerical results or text-described outcomes; cited findings from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests V3 through its own raw held-out accuracy comparisons between MLPs and convolutional networks trained from scratch with momentum SGD, including noisy-label settings and CIFAR-Easy. Its representation-probe comparisons measure a different outcome and do not themselves test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors argue that architecture aligned with the target function tends to preserve more predictive representations under noisy labels, while alignment with the noise can undermine them. They prove a restricted result and provide empirical evidence, and show that clean-label linear readouts can improve some noisy-label methods. Their robustness conclusion concerns representation predictive power and does not imply uniformly better raw model accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Studies robustness to noisy labels using representation probes and test performance, rather than random-label memorization, natural-label generalization, architecture width sweeps, or generalization-gap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with architecture alignment, dataset/task, noise type and ratio, and whether performance is measured on the raw model or a linear probe of its representations.

fits_no_version.finding: On graph tasks, target-aligned architectures retain linearly accessible target information under additive or instance-dependent noise, whereas alignment with the noise can impair recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural alignment with target and noise functions predicts representation robustness under noisy-label training.

fits_no_version.finding: CNN-based representations are generally more predictive on CIFAR-10/100, whereas MLP representations are more predictive on CIFAR-Easy; these probe rankings can differ from raw-accuracy rankings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The target function and architecture jointly determine how much clean-label information remains accessible to a linear probe after noisy-label training.

fits_no_version.finding: A probe using clean labels can substantially improve some DivideMix models, with failures and small gains in other conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Clean-label linear readouts can recover predictive performance from noisy-label models, depending on architectural alignment and noise type.

record.problems: The central robustness metric is probe performance using clean labels, not the trained model's own test error. Several comparisons are only described through figures without numerical values in prose. The paper notes that theoretical assumptions include sequential training, unlike its standard training procedure. Some CIFAR-Easy and graph-task results use synthetic labels or distributions.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many per-noise-ratio table entries and figure curves. Within the 60-row limit, detailed Table 1/2 entries were retained only for conditions emphasized in the text or showing especially large, small, or contrasting probe effects; most remaining Table 1/2 cells and individual points from Figures 3, 4, 7, and 8 are not separately represented. Table 3/4 random-initialization comparisons and Tables 5–10 comparisons with other noisy-label methods were omitted because they primarily assess probe outcomes against method baselines rather than separately stated raw-model-versus-probe effects relevant to the catalog versions.

untested.parts: No matched experiment establishes near-perfect fitting of fully random classification labels together with chance held-out performance and high natural-label performance under the same recipe. Partial label corruption is insufficient.
No width sweep past the width needed to interpolate.

No intervention isolates local connectivity, learned sparse local connections, or initialization of a fully connected network from a trained convolutional network. The study does not cover MNIST or SVHN.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison or tuning-budget comparison.
No controlled batch-size or fixed-epoch-budget comparison.
No dropout addition, removal, or strength comparison; dropout is an architecture component.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison of generalization-gap rankings.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization.

missing.what: Condition-specific vanilla raw-accuracy comparisons from Table 1 are missing from the rows' values. Record MLP, CNN, and ResNet accuracy separately from probe accuracy, including the high-uniform-noise reversals. These raw results underlie the V3 verdicts.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, Figure 7; Table 1, Vanilla training entries

missing.what: Separate vanilla raw-accuracy comparisons on CIFAR-Easy from probe outcomes and DivideMix comparisons. Table 2 supplies exact raw values establishing the MLP advantage under uniform and intermediate instance-dependent noise, together with equal or near-chance endpoint conditions.
missing.locator: Section 4.1, Figure 8; Table 2, Vanilla training entries

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. The extraction incorrectly excludes all V3 tests by focusing on probes and requiring clean-label training; raw architecture comparisons and the clean CIFAR-Easy sample-size experiment bear on V3. States for rows linked to none are cannot_determine relative to the catalog, not denials of the reported findings. Mixed rows require splitting before their states can represent every condition faithfully. Probe fitting also differs by architecture: ridge regression for MLPs and ordinary least squares for other models.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random labels with fitting natural labels or report held-out accuracy under random labels.
No width sweep beyond an interpolation threshold or test-error-versus-width result.
Compares CNN-based models and MLPs through representations under noisy labels, but does not test convolutional versus fully connected test error under standard clean-label training as stated.
No dropout intervention comparison for held-out error; dropout is part of the stated architecture details only.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
Does not remove memorized training examples or compare their removal with random-example removal.
